title: Cold Pan Chicken with Lemon Butter Pan Sauce
summary: Skin-on chicken started in a cold, dry pan so the fat renders slowly and the skin goes crisp. A pan sauce follows: shallot, garlic, white wine, stock, lemon and cold butter. Served with asparagus and potatoes.

steps.text: Salt the chicken, let it rest for 15 minutes, then pat it dry.
Put the chicken skin side down in a cold, empty pan. No oil.
Turn the heat to medium and wait. Season the top side now; she keeps it simple.
Let the fat render out. If the skin is still stuck to the pan, it isn't ready: leave it alone until it releases.
Flip and cook the other side, then take the chicken out to rest.

ingredients.amount: enough to cover the bottom of the pan

steps.text: Keep the browned bits (the fond) in the pan. Add the shallots, then the garlic, and stir briefly.
Deglaze with dry white wine, just enough to cover the bottom of the pan.
Add about 1 cup of chicken stock. Keep stirring while it reduces.
Once it has reduced, add a squeeze of lemon.
Turn the heat to low and stir in cold butter.
Plate the chicken with asparagus and potatoes and spoon the pan sauce over.

notes: The technique matches published cold-start guides: render the skin fat slowly, cold pan for skin and hot pan for crust, pat dry and salt first.
